en.name: Ice cream
en.summary: Ice cream keeps 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that — what runs out is texture, as ice crystals grow with every partial thaw and the smooth body turns grainy.
en.pantry: No room-temperature storage. Ice cream is a dairy product, and once melted it is milk: a soft, low-acid, high-protein food sitting in the danger zone of 4–60 °C (40–140 °F). Never refreeze a tub that has melted through, and do not leave one on the counter to soften — take it out for a few minutes only, or use a warm scoop. Melting and refreezing is also what produces the gritty, icy texture nobody wants.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is given, and the fridge is not a place to keep ice cream. Ice cream held at fridge temperature is simply melting slowly, and a melted dairy dessert that is then refrozen is both unpleasant and a genuine food-safety question, because it has spent time in the growth range. If you want it softer, move the tub to a warmer part of the freezer for a while, not to the fridge.
en.freezer: 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Keep the tub at the back of the freezer, never in the door: the door is where the temperature swings every time it opens, and each swing melts a fraction of the ice and refreezes it as a bigger crystal. That is the whole mechanism of ice cream going grainy. Press a piece of baking paper onto the surface before putting the lid back, which slows the ice crust that forms on top of a half-eaten tub.
en.thawing: Ice cream is not thawed — it is softened. Leave the tub at room temperature for a few minutes only, or run the scoop under hot water. A tub that has melted through should be thrown away rather than refrozen.
spoilage: A thick crust of ice crystals on the surface, or a grainy, sandy texture.
A shrunken tub with the ice cream pulled away from the sides — it melted and refroze.
A stale, cardboardy or freezer smell, or a taste of whatever else is in the freezer.
Any sour or off dairy smell, which means it goes out.
tips: Keep the tub at the back of the freezer, never in the door.
Press baking paper onto the surface of a half-eaten tub before replacing the lid.
Take it out for a few minutes rather than leaving it on the counter to soften.
Never refreeze ice cream that has melted through.

faq.q: How long does ice cream last in the freezer?
faq.a: 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe longer, but it turns grainy and icy.

faq.q: Can you refreeze melted ice cream?
faq.a: No. Melted ice cream is a dairy food that has been in the danger zone, and refreezing it also ruins the texture.

faq.q: Why has my ice cream gone icy and grainy?
faq.a: Temperature swings — usually from keeping it in the freezer door. Each partial melt refreezes into larger ice crystals.

zh.name: 冰淇淋
zh.summary: 冰淇淋在 −18 °C 下自購買日起可保有最佳品質 6 個月。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全——先用完的是口感：每一次半融化都會讓冰晶長大，綿密的質地慢慢變成粗粒。
zh.pantry: 沒有室溫保存這一項。冰淇淋是乳製品，融化之後它就是牛奶：一種柔軟、低酸、高蛋白，而且正待在 4～60 °C 危險溫度帶裡的食物。整桶融透的絕對不要再冷凍，也不要為了好挖就把它放在檯面上——只拿出來幾分鐘，或用溫熱過的挖杓。融化再結凍，也正是那種沒有人想要的沙沙口感的來源。
zh.fridge: 這裡不給冷藏期限，冷藏也不是放冰淇淋的地方。冰淇淋放在冷藏溫度下，就只是在慢慢融化而已；而一份融化過的乳製甜點再凍回去，既難吃也是真正的食安問題，因為它已經在生長溫度帶裡待過一段時間。想要它軟一點，就把整桶移到冷凍庫裡比較不冷的位置放一會兒，而不是移到冷藏。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下自購買日起 6 個月品質最好。整桶請放在冷凍櫃深處，絕對不要放門邊：門邊的溫度每開一次門就波動一次，而每一次波動都會融掉一小部分冰、再結成更大的冰晶。冰淇淋變粗糙的機制就是這個。吃剩的那桶，蓋回蓋子之前先在表面壓一張烘焙紙，可以拖慢表面那層冰殼。
zh.thawing: 冰淇淋不是拿來解凍的，是拿來回軟的。整桶在室溫放幾分鐘就好，或把挖杓用熱水沖一下。已經整桶融透的請丟掉，不要再凍回去。
spoilage: 表面結了厚厚一層冰晶，或口感變得粗粒、沙沙的。
冰淇淋從桶壁縮開、整體下陷——它融化過又再結凍。
聞起來走味、有紙板味或冷凍櫃的味道，甚至吃得出冷凍庫裡別的東西的味道。
出現任何乳製品的酸味或異味，那就該丟。
tips: 整桶放在冷凍櫃深處，絕對不要放門邊。
吃剩的那桶，蓋蓋子前先在表面壓一張烘焙紙。
只拿出來幾分鐘，不要擺在檯面上等它軟。
融透過的冰淇淋絕對不要再冷凍。

faq.a: −18 °C 下自購買日起 6 個月品質最好。只要沒退冰放更久仍然安全，但會變得又冰又粗。

faq.q: 融化的冰淇淋可以再冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 不行。融化的冰淇淋是待過危險溫度帶的乳製品，而且再凍回去口感也毀了。

faq.q: 冰淇淋為什麼變得沙沙的？
faq.a: 溫度波動造成的，通常是放在冷凍櫃門邊。每次半融化都會重新結成更大的冰晶。
